frequency_question: How often do countries under wartime conditions successfully establish domestic production of complex foreign-designed missile technology within ~2 years of need?
membership_rule: Members are sovereign nations engaged in active high-intensity conventional conflict that have received advanced foreign missile technology and attempted to domesticate its manufacturing lifecycle. Excludes simple licensed small-arms assembly or low-tech drone production.

cases.name: Taiwan establishing domestic production of Sky Bow systems with US tech transfer
Ukraine domestic production attempts of Soviet-design missiles post-2014
Iran reverse-engineering and producing variants of foreign anti-ship missiles under sanctions
Pakistan domestic production of certain foreign-sourced missile systems

coverage_note: 4 named historical analogs identified; highly specialized domain with few direct comparables.
known_gaps: Extremely sparse data due to classification of defense industrial base projects and unique technological hurdles of long-range cruise missiles.
validity_reason: Defense industrial base transfer timelines and manufacturing constraints evolve slowly over decades.
